meta.description:
The primary mission of the 436 CES Pavements and Construction Equipment Section is to construct, maintain, inspect, and repair horizontal infrastructure across the installation. This includes airfields, roadways, perimeter security barriers, and drainage networks.
The section provides 24/7/365 rapid response and all-weather airfield capability, ensuring zero downtime for Dover AFB’s strategic airlift fleet (C-5M Super Galaxy and C-17 Globemaster III). Their continuous operations directly enable the projection of sovereign power, high-priority humanitarian relief, international foreign military sales, and the solemn transfer of fallen American service members.

meta.jhaNotes:
BE Survey Notes: Dover AFB high-risk workplace (20 personnel) maintaining roads and flightlines. Measured Noise (98.6 dBA) and Silica (Quartz/Total Respirable: ~0.28 mg/m3) exposures are significantly above OEL.

JHA Findings & Major Hazards: Hazardous noise from heavy equipment, pneumatic tools, and flightline operations; respirable crystalline silica during demolition/cutting operations; Methanol skin absorption during weekly vehicle disassembly.

Controls: Double hearing protection (plugs and muffs); 3M 7800S respirators; chemical splash goggles; mandatory administrative training (silica, respiratory protection, heat/cold stress, hearing conservation).

Special Restrictions: Fetal Protection Program requires pregnant personnel to report immediately to Public Health for workplace evaluations, restriction recommendations (AF Form 422), and briefings. Shop supervisors not requiring exams have a 0.00 dBA Noise E

meta.medicalFacility:
1. 🚑 Ambulance & Emergency Response (Life, Limb, or Eyesight)
Immediate Call: Dial 911 (or 302-677-3333 if calling from a cellular device on base) .

On-Base Response: Emergency medical dispatch coordinates through the Dover AFB Emergency Communication Center. On base, emergency medical response is provided 24/7 by the Ambulance Response Team (ART) (436th Medical Group / Civil Engineer Squadron Fire Station) in coordination with local Kent County/City of Dover EMS .

Actions On Scene:
State your exact building number (e.g., Bldg 615 / Horizontal Construction Shop), specific shop area/bay, and nature of injury.

Direct someone to flag down the emergency vehicle at the hangar/bay apron or street entrance.

For chemical contamination (e.g., methanol, solvent splashes, silica in eyes), begin immediate flushing at the eyewash station/drench shower and inform dispatch of the chemical involved.

2. 🏥 Hospital & Emergency Room (Off-Base)
The 436th Medical Group Clinic on base does NOT have an Emergency Room . For severe trauma, life-threatening injuries, or after-hours emergencies requiring hospital care:
Primary Designated Emergency Room:
Bayhealth Hospital, Kent Campus (Kent General)

Address: 640 S. State St., Dover, DE 19901

Phone: (302) 674-4700

Reporting Requirement: If an active duty member is admitted to or treated at a civilian emergency department, notify the Primary Care Manager (PCM) / Flight Medicine and the workplace supervisor within 24 hours to ensure authorization and documentation .

3. 🩺 Outpatient Clinic Procedures (436th Medical Group)
Location: Building 300, Tuskegee Blvd, Dover AFB .

Routine & Occupational Care:
Appointment Line: Call (302) 730-4633 .

Occupational Health / Bioenvironmental / Public Health: Coordinates annual medical surveillance, audiograms, respirator clearances, and fetal protection program restrictions .

Non-Emergency After-Hours:
Call the MHS Nurse Advice Line at 1-800-TRICARE (874-2273) prior to seeking off-base urgent care to avoid unauthorized medical billing

meta.shelterInPlace:
Tornado / Severe Weather Shelter-in-Place
When a Tornado Warning is issued for Dover AFB, immediately move to designated structural shelters:
Primary Shelter Location: The locker rooms, restrooms, or interior administrative hallways of the facility. These are structural load-bearing concrete/block areas located away from exterior walls, windows, and high-span hangar roof hazard points.

Prohibited Areas (DO NOT Shelter Here):
Avoid the main vehicle bays/hangar garage spaces. High-clearance ceilings and large overhead bay doors are highly susceptible to structural failure, high-wind collapse, and flying debris hazards.

Avoid any exterior-facing office spaces with windows.

☣️ Chemical, Biological, Radiological, or Nuclear (CBRN) / Hazardous Release SIP
If an airborne hazard (e.g., toxic chemical spill, flightline fuel release, or off-base industrial accident) requires sheltering in place to avoid contaminated outside air:
Primary Shelter Location: Designated Interior Breakroom or Office Space that can be rapidly sealed.

Immediate Actions:
Seal the Room: Close all interior doors and windows.

Isolate Ventilation: Turn off all HVAC/exhaust systems, window fans, and air conditioning units immediately to prevent drawing in contaminated outside air.

Seal Gaps: If a CBRN kit is available, use heavy plastic sheeting and duct tape to block under-door drafts and vents .

📋 Shelter-in-Place Responsibilities
Supervisors: Ensure a head count is taken immediately once the shop is sheltered.

Communication: Monitor the Giant Voice (base siren), desktop pop-up alerts, or the Command Post frequency (302-677-4201) for official "All Clear" messages.
meta.activeShooterMethods:
🏃‍♂️ 1. RUN (Evacuate)
If there is an accessible escape path, attempt to evacuate the premises immediately.
Action: Evacuate the shop floor or office space and run to a safe distance away from the facility.

Flightline & Yards: If you are outdoors on the vehicle apron or concrete yards, seek immediate cover behind heavy earthmoving equipment, concrete barriers, or masonry walls.

Guidelines:
Leave your belongings behind.

Keep your hands visible, empty, and raised above your head to show Security Forces responder teams that you are unarmed.

Prevent others from entering the area if safe to do so.

🚪 2. HIDE (Barricade)
If evacuation is not possible, find a place to hide where the active shooter is less likely to find you.
Best Locations in Bldg 615:
Locked administrative offices, restrooms, or utility/storage rooms.

Tool Cribs / Secure Supply Cages: These areas often feature heavy metal lock doors that can act as formidable physical barriers.

Barricade & Secure:
Lock the door and block it using heavy office furniture, filing cabinets, or structural tools.

Turn off the lights, silence all cell phones (turn off vibrate mode), and remain completely quiet.

Stay out of the shooter's line of sight through door windows or sidelights.

🛠️ 3. FIGHT (Defend)
As a last resort, and only when your life is in imminent danger, attempt to disrupt or incapacitate the active shooter.
Action: Act with maximum physical aggression. Throw items, improvised weapons, and commit to your actions.

Improvised Shop Weapons: The Horizontal Construction shop contains heavy, solid tools (wrenches, pry bars, shovels, heavy flashlights) that can be utilized to defend your life if cornered.
📞 Contacting Security Forces (SFS)
Once you are in a safe or secure position, dial 911 or 302-677-3333 (Dover Base Dispatch) / 302-677-6664 (SFS Desk).

Provide the operator with your exact location (Building 615 / Horizontal Construction), number of shooters, physical description, and types of weapons observed.
meta.adverseWeatherShelter:
🌪️ Tornado Warnings & High Wind Events
In the event of a tornado warning, severe thunderstorm warning, or extreme high-wind advisory (gusts exceeding 50+ knots) on Dover AFB, immediately seek shelter within Building 615 or nearest hardened facility:
Primary Shelter Location: The locker rooms, restrooms, or central interior hallways. These areas are constructed with heavy concrete/masonry walls and do not have exterior windows or doors.

Prohibited Hazard Zones:
Main Vehicle & Heavy Equipment Bays: DO NOT remain in the large open bays or maintenance garages. The wide-span roofing and large overhead bay doors are highly susceptible to buckling, collapsing, or letting in high-velocity flying debris.

Offices with Windows: Avoid any office space with windows or glass sidelights.

⚡ Lightning Events (Lightning Within 5 Nautical Miles)
The flightline and open concrete yards utilized by Horizontal Construction are highly vulnerable to lightning strikes.
Action: Immediately halt all outdoor work, flightline maintenance, and concrete pouring.

Shelter: Move indoors to Building 615.

Heavy Equipment Warning: Large earthmovers, graders, and dump trucks do not guarantee total lightning safety. Get inside a fully enclosed metal-cab vehicle with windows rolled up if a building is inaccessible, and avoid touching any exposed interior metal connected to the frame.

❄️ Winter Storms & Extreme Cold
Horizontal Construction personnel are critical for winter airfield operations (snow and ice removal):
Shelter Strategy: Utilize the administrative breakrooms to cycle personnel through warm environments during extended snow-clearing operations.

Monitoring: Ensure buddy checks are actively performed to monitor for signs of frostbite or hypothermia.

🚨 Base Weather Alerts & Communications
Monitor the Giant Voice (outdoor siren system).

Keep a shop computer open to the AtHoc emergency notification pop-ups.

If communication lines are needed, contact the Civil Engineer (CE) Control Center or the Dover AFB Weather Flight at 302-677-2705 / 302-677-4201 (Command Post).
meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
For Horizontal Construction (Dirtboyz) personnel operating heavy equipment, dump trucks, and standard government motor vehicles (GMVs) around Dover AFB, local traffic hazards and specific vehicle guidelines are structured as follows:
🚪 Local Gate Hazards & Traffic Concerns

 Area / Hazard Point	Specific Risk & Action Required
Main Gate (Main / North Gate) 🚧	High-volume commercial and POV traffic. Heavy equipment transit is restricted during peak hours (0630-0830 and 1530-1730). Use caution when navigating barriers designed for Force Protection.
Commercial Gate (South Gate) 🚛	Primary entry point for construction deliveries and oversized loads. Watch for blind spots, slow-turning semi-trucks, and security check queues blocking the lane.
Airfield / Flightline Access Gates ✈️	FOD (Foreign Object Damage) Hazards: Ensure tires are checked and cleared of stones or debris before entering airfield access points. Ground equipment must yield to all taxiing aircraft and emergency response vehicles.
Pavement Maintenance Zones ⚠️	Transition zones between gravel yards and paved base roads. Mud and debris tracked onto public base roads by heavy equipment must be cleared immediately to prevent motorcycle and vehicle slippage.

 📞 Safety Contacts
Base Safety Office (436 AW/SE): 302-677-2204 (For reporting roadway safety hazards or vehicle mishaps)

Security Forces Desk (SFS dispatch): 302-677-6664 (For traffic control, escort assistance, or road blockages)

CE Control Center (U-Drive): 302-677-4654 (For local road maintenance and heavy vehicle routing coordination)
Vehicle Training & Documentation
To legally operate GMVs and specialized construction equipment, training must be explicitly tracked and documented:
AF Form 2293 (USAF Motor Vehicle Operator Identification Card): Must be carried by the operator, detailing every specific class of equipment they are authorized to operate (e.g., graders, loaders, dump trucks).

AF Form 483 (Flightline Driver's License): Must be in possession of any operator driving on the airfield flightline, complete with current annual flightline driver training certification

selectedModules.title: Hazard Communication
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train personnel on hazardous chemicals in their work area, labeling systems, safety data sheets, and the measures they can take to protect themselves during normal operations and foreseeable emergencies.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide HazCom training upon initial assignment, whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced, and when new tasks expose workers to different hazardous materials. Ensure workers know how to access local SDS information and labeling guidance.

selectedModules.title: Hearing Conservation
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train noise-exposed employees annually on the effects of noise, the purpose of hearing protectors, the advantages and disadvantages of various protectors, and the purpose of audiometric testing.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure workers enrolled in hearing conservation understand noise hazard areas, double-hearing protection requirements, and local follow-up actions tied to occupational health evaluations.

selectedModules.title: Manual and Powered Hoists
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 35
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide task-specific training on safe use, load limits, inspections, and operating procedures before workers use hoists in material handling operations.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local lesson plans or manufacturer instructions to cover pre-use inspections, operator limitations, suspended-load controls, and maintenance reporting requirements.

selectedModules.title: Respiratory Protection Program
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train users before respirator use and at least annually on why the respirator is necessary, how improper fit or maintenance can compromise protection, and how to inspect, don, doff, use, and store the respirator.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Document fit testing and occupational health training on AF Form 2767 and ensure wearers understand emergency-use limits, cartridge change-out, cleaning, and medical qualification requirements.

selectedModules.title: Forklift / Material Handling Equipment
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 35; 29 CFR 1910.178 - Powered industrial trucks
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train powered industrial truck operators in truck-related and workplace-related topics, evaluate performance, and conduct refresher training when unsafe operation, incidents, or workplace changes occur.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use approved lesson plans, hands-on evaluation, and recurring reevaluation before certifying operators. Cover spotter requirements, aircraft proximity rules, and local route restrictions.

selectedModules.title: CPR Training
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 1
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide CPR and AED training before assignment where required, and refresh qualification before expiration.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Ensure designated responders maintain current certification and understand location and use of local AED assets under the unit mishap prevention program.
selectedModules.notes: Hands on class members every 2 years

selectedModules.title: Ladder Safety
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 7
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers to inspect ladders before use, maintain three points of contact, set ladders on stable surfaces, and avoid overreaching or using damaged ladders.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide hands-on ladder safety training at first assignment, including local storage, damaged-tag procedures, and fall prevention expectations.

selectedModules.title: Active Shooter Response
selectedModules.reference: Installation emergency management guidance / local procedures
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Brief personnel on how to recognize an active shooter event, how to summon help, and how to apply local run-hide-fight guidance based on the facility layout.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local emergency response procedures, shelter locations, and mass notification methods applicable to the duty location.

selectedModules.title: Government Vehicle / Utility Vehicle Use
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train vehicle operators on seat belts, speed limits, local traffic hazards, spotter use while backing, and restrictions on electronic device use while driving.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Brief operators on unit-specific government vehicle training requirements, local route restrictions, low-speed vehicle rules, and documentation of qualification.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Vehicle and Mobile Equipment Concepts

selectedModules.title: Manual Lifting and Material Handling
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 20
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers on proper lifting techniques, team lifting, load assessment, and use of lifting aids to reduce musculoskeletal injury risk.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Provide verbal and written guidance on manual lifting, lifting devices, and local reporting actions for strain or overexertion symptoms.
selectedModules.trainingBasis: OSHA 2254 / Ergonomics and Material Handling Concepts

selectedModules.title: Jewelry / Loose Articles Restrictions
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train workers on removing jewelry and securing loose articles when working around machinery, electrical hazards, rotating equipment, or snag hazards.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use local work-center restrictions and equipment guidance to define prohibited items and exceptions for mission-essential tasks.

selectedModules.title: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards, Chapter 14; 29 CFR Part 1910 - Occupational Safety and Health Standards (General Industry Standards) Subpart I; 29 CFR 1910.132; 29 CFR 1910.133; 29 CFR 1910.135; 29 CFR 1910.136; 29 CFR 1910.138
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train each affected worker on when PPE is necessary, what PPE is necessary, how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE, the limitations of assigned PPE, and the proper care, maintenance, useful life, and disposal of PPE. Require workers to demonstrate understanding and proper use before performing work requiring PPE, and retrain when workplace conditions, job assignments, PPE types, or worker knowledge gaps make prior training obsolete.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the work-center JHA, BE occupational health assessment, manufacturer instructions, DAFMAN 91-203 Chapter 14, and local safety office guidance to identify PPE requirements. Supervisors must ensure PPE is provided, used, cleaned, inspected, maintained in sanitary and serviceable condition, and documented in JSTO training records. Cover eye and face protection, head protection, foot protection, hand protection, protective clothing, and respiratory or hearing protection when those programs apply.
